title: Attention hybrid fusion: hardware affinity triage
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working triage notebook to capture experiments, observations, and next steps for a recurring tail-latency regression we've observed on mixed workloads that use the hybrid attention path: FlashAttention (when available) + paged-attention fallback + fused ops. The symptom: intermittent p95/p99 spikes (2–6x baseline) for medium-length sequences (seq_len 256–1024) under small-batch concurrent traffic (batch 1–8, concurrency 40–120).

Quick executive summary (working):
- Repro: Stable on single-process synthetic runner with sampled live prompts. Spikes correlate with sudden model mix changes (switching from short to medium sequences) and with host CPU load increases.
- Root causes (hypothesis): dynamic kernel switch thrash (kernel selection jitter), page fault/host->GPU staging from paged-attn, and suboptimal kernel-to-SM affinity for our fused-attn kernels causing occupancy drops.
- Short-term mitigations: pin kernel-selection decision for duration of request group; increase prefetch window for paged-attn; enforce NUMA/cpu-affinity for worker threads on nodes with high host utilization.
- Medium-term: add kernel affinity policy in runtime (prefer flash on warm SMs, avoid repeated fusion/unfusion within microbatch), add sampling to model switch code path, tune threshold heuristics for kernel fallback.

Environment and test harness:
- HW: NVIDIA A100-SXM4 80GB (4-card nodes), PCIe host in some clusters.
- SW: CUDA 11.8, cuDNN 8.2, PyTorch 2.1, custom serving-runtime v0.42.1 + attention-plugin branch.
- Toolkit: nsight-systems (nsys 2023.5), NVIDIA Nsight Compute (ncu), perf, /proc/interrupts, dmesg, and our tracebench harness.
- Workloads: synthetic-parity runner that replays real requests sampled from prod; controlled mix: {short: seq 32 (60%), medium: seq 512 (30%), long: seq 2048 (10%)}.

Experiment 1 — kernel-selection churn profiling (nsys traces):
- Setup: concurrent clients = 80, batch_size=4, model=mix-llama-like-7b, baseline kernel policy = dynamic (runtime chooses flash vs paged).
- Command: nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --output=trace_1 npx runbench --mix-config ...
- Observations: many requests show 2–5 kernel launches in <2 ms window: flash_attn_fp16 -> fused_attn_v2 -> paged_attn_page_load (reversed)
- Metric excerpts (from trace aggregation):
  - mean kernel launches / request: 2.9
  - requests with >3 kernel launches: 17%
  - p99 tail where >3 launches: 380 ms (major contributor to observed tail spikes)
- Micro-hypothesis: kernel policy uses heuristic based on recent sequence length distribution but sampling interval is too short; when mix shifts, the runtime flips selection mid-request group causing cache thrash and extra prefetch/teardown.

Experiment 2 — paged-attention page-load cost breakdown (ncu + mem stats):
- Setup: isolate medium sequences only, run with paged-attn enabled.
- Observations:
  - page-load kernel (paged_attn_page_load) shows high DRAM throughput and stalls on mem_dependency_count.
  - Host-side observed page faults rare, but when host CPU load climbs, the page load kernel is starved behind CPU-driven DMA scheduling causing jitter.
- Latency samples:
  - paged_attn_page_load median = 3.2 ms, p95 = 9.8 ms, p99 = 24.1 ms (with noisy host)
- Micro-hypothesis: paged-attn benefits from prefetching multiple pages ahead; current prefetch window (w=1) is too conservative. Increasing to w=3 reduces p99 to ~8–10 ms in noisy host tests.

Experiment 3 — fused ops kernel affinity and SM occupancy (ncu):
- Setup: run fused_op kernels with synthetic streams that vary SM utilization. Inject CPU background load to cause warps scheduling skew.
- Observations:
  - fused_attn_v2 shows occupancy drop from 72% -> 38% under certain launch parameters (grid/block mismatch for variable seq).
  - ncu reveals increased warp_serialize and bank_conflicts on lanes where sequence modulo causes alignment shifts.
  - When we pin the CUDA stream to a GPU subset and reserve SMs (via cudaDeviceSetLimit + test shim), observed stable occupancy and lower p99.
- Metric excerpts:
  - fused_attn_v2 single-kernel runtime: median 1.8 ms, p95 5.2 ms (unrestricted), after affinity hinting: median 1.6 ms, p95 2.1 ms.
- Micro-hypothesis: the fused kernels are sensitive to where they land on SMs due to shared L2/cache reuse; runtime’s current schedule allows interleaving with other kernels that evict shared caches, leading to repeated global loads. Kernel placement/stream isolation helps.

Synthesis of findings:
- Two orthogonal contributors: (1) dynamic kernel-switch thrash that causes extra kernel launches + data motion, (2) paged-attn page-load variability amplified by host scheduling and small prefetch window. A third amplifying factor is kernel affinity/SM placement that increases cache misses and warp serialization when fused ops run in noisy multi-tenant environment.

Quick fixes we tried and results:
- Increasing paged-attn prefetch window to 3: reduced paged page-load p99 by ~60% on noisy hosts (tradeoff: ~6% extra memory footprint).
- Coalescing kernel selection decisions per microbatch (pin decision for N=8 requests): reduced kernel launch churn from mean 2.9 -> 1.1; tail p99 reduced by ~45% on mixed workloads.
- Stream isolation for fused kernels (separate cudaStream per model instance / soft-reservation): improved fused kernel p95 by ~60% in our tests.

Implementation notes for runtime changes (practical):
- Add a short-lived sticky decision: when model route transitions are detected, freeze kernel selection for the duration of current microbatch group (configurable TTL, default 50 ms).
- Add adaptive paged prefetch: start with w=1 and increase to w=3 when host RT latency > X or when paged-attn p95 > threshold. This can be a runtime knob per-customer.
- Kernel affinity policy: implement soft-affinity by assigning model instances to CUDA-stream pools and prefer reusing same stream/SM neighborhood for subsequent batches. Avoid strict hard partitioning (too heavy) — use scheduler hints.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Interaction with multi-GPU model parallelism: does affinity help or hurt when KV cache shards are spread across GPUs? Need cross-node experiments.
- Does SM reservation (via driver-level API or cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel) provide stable improvements at scale, or is it brittle under packing?
- What is the memory cost of increased paged prefetch at 99th percentile for our largest model family (13B+/seq 4096)? Run mem-pressure simulation.

Action items (next week):
1) Marcus: implement kernel-selection sticky TTL in runtime (small PR), add feature flag + telemetry. (ETA 4d)
2) Priya: run paged-prefetch matrix for w in {1,2,3,4} across model sizes with stress CPU background (use stress-ng). Produce a table of memory delta vs p99 latency. (ETA 5d)
3) Ethan: prototype stream-pool affinity scheduler and benchmark fused-attn kernels at concurrency 80/160 on A100 nodes with mixed model shapes. (ETA 7d)
4) Aisha: create Canary rollout plan to test sticky policy behind a flag for 10% of traffic and monitor p50/p95/p99 server-side and cost delta. (ETA 3d)

Appendix — useful command snippets:
- nsys: nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o /tmp/trace.nsight --sample=none --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx python -m bench.run --mix ...
- ncu (kernel-level): ncu --target-processes=all --metrics l1tex__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_wavefront0.avg.pct,l2_subp0_read_throughput --kernel-id ::fused_attn_v2 --launch-skip 0 --launch-count 50 --csv --log-file ncu_fused.csv ./runner
- basic runtime log knobs: RUNTIME_ATTENTION_PREFETCH_WINDOW=3 RUNTIME_KERNEL_STICKY_TTL_MS=50 RUNTIME_STREAM_POOL=enabled

Notes to self: keep this doc live during the triage; move to a final postmortem once mitigations are released. Capture telemetry dashboards iframe links in Confluence doc.

End of notebook (draft).
